minutes.headline: Planning Board continued the 494 Electric Ave and three Lemonster/Kilburn storm water hearings pending peer review, and approved the 1260 Reservoir Rd site plan.
minutes.summary: The board heard from the applicant and many neighbors on the 494 Electric Avenue parking and commercial building project, with concerns about flooding, traffic, lighting and noise, and a dispute over whether the town ever took Pierce Avenue. It voted to fund peer review and continued all four hearings to November 25. It approved the PJ Keating site plan, signed two decisions, and approved a certificate of completion.

public_comment.stated_role: owner of 480 Electric Avenue and 15 Kirby Avenue
public_comment.topic: Gutters at the new building at El Forno discharge onto the rear of 15 Kirby Ave and flood it; also noise from live entertainment.
Asked about the buffer, lighting, egress, traffic study and why so many parking spaces.
Flooding at the end of the street since the lot was disturbed.
Private road plowing and runoff from the earlier El Forno building; wanted to show a video.
Quality of the wall, high water table, bright lights, and her water shutoff location.
Water, Pierce Ave traffic, and lighting.
Parking and traffic on Pierce Ave; water.
Asked about the WHM overlay district, drainage and snow storage.
Water in basements; asked about catch basins and grading.
Asked whether comment applied to 70 Kilburn; later raised flooding of the curve and driveway safety.
Storm water pooling and icing on Lemonster Road near the proposed lots.
Staff member Logan suggested posting meeting dates and filing deadlines publicly in advance; board supported it.

what_happened.line: The board voted to fund an outside peer review for the 494 Electric Avenue parking and commercial building project, paid by the applicant.
All four hearings, 494 Electric Avenue, 791 and 795 Lemonster Road and 70 Kilburn Street, were continued to November 25 pending peer review.
For the three storm water hearings on Lemonster Road and Kilburn Street, the board required peer review, with an applicant deposit to the town's 53G account.
The board approved the 1260 Reservoir Road site plan with standard conditions and did not require peer review.
The board approved a certificate of completion for the 319 Highland Street storm water permit and signed two decisions.

why_it_matters: Neighbors of 494 Electric Avenue raised flooding, traffic, lighting and noise, and the independent engineering review that now follows is meant to test the drainage before the board decides.

The town has no money of its own to pay peer reviewers, so applicant deposits to the 53G account decide whether a storm water review happens, and a fee schedule revision is meant to make applicant fees cover the department's budget.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on all eleven non-procedural votes: the same motions, the same $5,000 and $3,000 amounts, the same 25 November continuations, with the vote count and every name matching once caption errors are resolved. They differ mainly on decisions and detail. Our minutes have the peer-review and certificate-of-completion practice decisions, the "53G" deposit wording and a $15,000 figure that the official minutes lack. The official minutes have the applicant-side attendees, the public commenters, the title-search request and the setback-waiver review that our minutes lack. They also record the 255 Sunny Hill vote as 2-2, with a date that does not fit this meeting.
